tagline: Down from Tye River Gap with the river for company.
intro: At Tye River Gap on the Blue Ridge Parkway, Route 56 becomes the Crabtree Falls Highway and starts down through Montebello, following the South Fork of the Tye past Crabtree Falls to Nash, where it picks up the Tye River proper. Just west of Tyro it leaves the national forest for gentler ground and keeps to the river through Massies Mill to Roseland.

Other Nelson County roads belong to the same byway. Beech Grove Road climbs to the Parkway at Reeds Gap, and Rockfish River Road runs toward Schuyler, where Earl Hamner Jr. grew up and found the material for The Waltons.

moments.title: Crabtree Falls
moments.text: A Forest Service trail leads to Crabtree Falls, five major cascades in all, the tallest of them dropping about 400 feet, before the water goes on to the Tye.

moments.title: Tyro
moments.text: Tyro takes its name from the English word for a beginner, and its frame grist mill of the 1840s keeps its wooden gears, overshot wheel and two runs of millstones.

moments.title: Massies Mill
moments.text: In August 1969 the remnants of Hurricane Camille came down on Massies Mill, then a village of forty homes, while its people slept.
